failure_summary.description: Chose the bare or hedged prefix option (trapezoidal only; 'moreover' clause dropped; 'need not hold' tail) over an extension whose extra clause survives a cheap test.

Chose the lone option that dropped the constant's dependence list (C=C(p,q,n)), or that used sum N_c in place of sum c·N_c (forces finitely many breathers). Every other option agreed on the dissenting clause.

In 'equivalent to' stems, chose a level-shifted or newly-named-object reformulation (Σ^1_2 vs Σ^1_1; LRB/RRB criterion that restates the stem's own hypothesis) over the same-level, plain-vocabulary equivalent.
Group-theoretic splitting criterion; knowledge-bound, with no clear structural cue.

patch.reasoning: Six of eight wrong answers were the same kind of option: the bare, hedged or dependence-free variant that the other options extend or contradict. The skill already says not to default to bare options, but the Final sanity pass still pushes toward 'the plainer option', and the odd-one-out rule is limited to coefficient or index placement. The edits are short and replace existing text instead of adding a long checklist, since the earlier long checklist was rejected. (1) Generalise the odd-one-out rule into an explicit clause vote plus a prefix check, so the lone dissenter on a clause and the common-weakening prefix are both flagged with a concrete procedure. (2) Remove the Final sanity pass's pull toward the plainer option when that option is a prefix of several others. (3) State when 'there exists C' placed after 'for every u' is non-uniform and cannot be equivalent to a fixed-constant inequality. (4) Add a same-level, same-vocabulary cue for equivalence stems against level-shifted or restated-hypothesis reformulations.

edits.target: - When options differ only by where a coefficient or index sits (λ on the s_1 term vs the s_2 term, A before B, i vs j), count how many options use each placement. If one option is the isolated swap and all others agree on the other placement, the swap is the corruption (distractors are single edits of the truth and so mostly inherit its details). Confirm with the stem's naming order or a limiting case (a parameter → 0) when possible.
edits.content:
- Clause vote (write it out before ranking): for each atomic clause (constant or dependence list, weight such as sum N_c vs sum c·N_c, level or index, range, a 'Moreover' clause, a tail like 'need not' / 'only'), note the wording each option uses. Distractors are single edits of the truth, so the truth agrees with the majority on every clause. An option that is the lone dissenter where all the others agree (it alone drops the dependence list, changes a weight, omits the 'Moreover' clause, or adds a 'need not' tail) is presumed corrupted. Overturn this only with a derivation. The bare, hedged or dependence-free variant is often listed last, and its position earns no credit.
- Prefix check: if one option's text appears verbatim inside two or more others, it is their common weakening. Do not take it as the safe base. Give each extension one cheap test (degenerate case, cheap invariant, does it silently change a stem hypothesis) and take the extension whose extras survive. An extra that contradicts an equality case (a strict inequality on a constant stretch) or is only an 'asymptotic / for large indices' downgrade is the corrupted one. Keep the bare option only if every extension fails. When the dissent is a changed placement of a coefficient or index (λ on s_1 vs s_2, A before B), the lone placement is the swap; confirm with the stem's naming order or a limiting case.

edits.target: If your choice carries the extra, more specific, or more elaborate clause and you only have a plausibility argument for it, switch to the plainer option unless that option is demonstrably false or strictly implied by a fully proved alternative.
edits.content: If your choice carries an extra clause that you cannot derive or that fails a test, switch to the plainer option. Do this only if the plainer option is not a verbatim prefix of two or more other options (then compare the extensions per the clause vote and take the one whose extras survive), and it is not demonstrably false or strictly implied by a fully proved alternative.

edits.target: Equally, a vague 'some C' is often a weakened distractor. Decide by checking against the stem, not by default.
edits.content: Equally, a vague 'some C' is often a weakened distractor. In an 'equivalent to' stem whose target inequality has one fixed constant, an option of the form 'for every solution/function u ... there exists C>0' lets C depend on u (non-uniform, nearly vacuous) and cannot be equivalent. The faithful option names a constant depending only on the structural parameters of the stem (e.g. C=C(p,q,n)) and keeps the stem's exponents, norms and ranges. If the other options all state the dependence list, the lone option omitting it is the weakened one.

edits.target: ## Trivial directions, negative hedges, iff vs one-way, FPT vs XP
edits.content: - Equivalence stems: the true equivalent sits at the same level as the stem's own object and is phrased in the stem's vocabulary (same complexity class or index, same family of bounds, a neighbouring plain bound). An option that shifts the level or index (Σ^1_1 → Σ^1_2, k → k+1), introduces newly named subobjects as a 'criterion', or restates the stem's own hypothesis as part of the conclusion is an inflated reformulation. Take it only if you can derive both directions.
